channel.title: Responsible AI & Neurodivergence, Naba Rizvi
channel.description: Daily curated research feed on ethical and responsible AI, with emphasis on neurodivergent people and serious mental illness.

item.title: AccessEval: Benchmarking Disability Bias in Large Language Models
item.description: AccessEval pairs neutral and disability aware versions of the same query across six real world domains and nine disability types, then evaluates twenty one closed and open models on sentiment, social perception and factual accuracy. Disability aware queries draw more negative tone, more stereotyping and higher factual error, and the size of the gap varies by domain, with disabilities affecting hearing, speech and mobility disproportionately impacted. Because the domains are decision making contexts rather than abstract probes, the results connect measured bias to tangible harms for disabled users instead of leaving it as a score.

item.title: Beyond Keywords: Evaluating Large Language Model Classification of Nuanced Ableism
item.description: The authors test whether four models can recognise ableism aimed at autistic people, separating the question of whether a model knows the relevant terminology from whether it can see harm in context. Models identify autism related language reliably but miss the harmful or offensive connotation, leaning on surface keyword matching where human annotators weigh context, speaker identity and likely impact. The consequence is practical rather than theoretical: systems used for content moderation or filtering risk censoring autistic community voices while overlooking subtle harm aimed at them.

item.title: Shiny Stories, Hidden Struggles: Investigating the Representation of Disability Through the Lens of LLMs
item.description: Models were asked to write social media posts in the voice of people with disabilities, and the results were compared against posts written by real disabled people on emotional tone, sentiment and recurring themes. The models idealize disabled experience, producing uplifting stereotypes that read well and miss lived reality. A second comparison between simulated disabled and non disabled authors exposes a negative bias in topic allocation, with subjects such as career and entertainment disproportionately assigned to non disabled personas.

item.title: Medicare Advantage Insurers Face New Bipartisan Scrutiny Over AI and Care Denials
item.description: Senators Blumenthal and Hawley asked UnitedHealth Group, Humana and CVS Health for internal records on how artificial intelligence is used to block or delay rehabilitative care, arriving a month after an inspector general investigation found a continuing pattern of denials inside Medicare Advantage. The lawmakers argue those findings undercut insurer claims to have reduced barriers to crucial services. Rehabilitative care sits at the centre of disability access, so automated prior authorisation is where algorithmic accountability turns into a coverage question rather than an abstract one.
